samples.marker_line: ltidisafe 4.0.3: covert preinstall host identity exfiltration
samples.reason: Unrelated OS identifiers are covertly transmitted during npm preinstall. The exported NetworkSpeedCheck library can perform ordinary caller-selected throughput tests, but test.js makes three unsolicited requests with hex-encoded username, hostname and home-directory DNS labels to an OAST callback. package.json executes it before install with both output streams discarded. This is an install-time reconnaissance/exfiltration package. An authorized security assessment could explain the callback, but no such deployment evidence or consent is supplied; the automatic silent hook tips the balance.
reverse_engineering: index.js exports NetworkSpeedCheck. _protocol selects http or https from the supplied URL. checkDownloadSpeed invokes GET and computes throughput from response data/end timestamps. checkUploadSpeed sends generated random JSON through http.request; it does not send a local file.

test.js imports that class, calls os.hostname(), os.homedir(), os.userInfo().username and converts each value through Buffer.from(utf8).toString(hex). getNetworkDownloadSpeedData concatenates its data parameter into the callback hostname and hands the constructed URL to checkDownloadSpeed. Module-level calls send username, hostname and home directory separately.

os.networkInterfaces() is queried and noninternal IPv4 addresses are assigned to localip. localip is never sent. Uptime query/send code is commented out; do not claim either uptime or interface-address exfiltration.

A bounded QuickJS context with JS-only HTTP, OS and Buffer stubs records exactly three GET requests whose DNS labels decode to the substituted username, hostname and home directory. The original package and test source were evaluated only against those stubs; no native host bridges or network capabilities were exposed.

samples.marker_line: Nikki Stealer JS: token theft; fix labels, add ZIP/AEAD traits
samples.reason: The sample is a Nikki Stealer-branded Node credential harvester, not a normal library. Its recovered entry point leads to Discord session-token acquisition and validation, browser-secret decryption, covert reporting, Discord module replacement and an attempted Startup executable copy. File and wallet collection routines further support its malicious purpose. No consent, research-package wrapper, package identity/version or deployment context is supplied. The supplied source is damaged and cannot execute as-is; that affects reachability and success, not the evident purpose of its preserved code.
reverse_engineering: The original begins with a function-shaped body missing the function keyword and ends with an unterminated JSON fragment ({ followed by a partial name key). Source boundaries were repaired only in scratch for parsing, never in the supplied sample.

goOJ5X returns an LZW-compressed string table. m1PAyrg performs dictionary decompression and splits the result on |, yielding 1087 entries. a1O6NM indexes these values; UIQwte implements Base91 decoding of 1028 strings. sentimentos assembles a second string table, and the checksum rotation yields 463 strings addressed by querome(index-483).

Only codec helpers, table initialization, arithmetic helpers and rotation were evaluated inside bounded QuickJS contexts with no host bridges. The payload entry point was never executed. Decoder calls were replaced with literals and decoded strings normalized to inspect the code and call chains.

dEiCe awaits SuiCidar, DEIce, faLar, NIKki, sUIcidar and queRome, triggers a dispatcher that invokes CheGa, then calls sEnTimentos. SuiCidar obtains tasklist through child_process.execSync and issues forced taskkill commands for Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave and Telegram when found.

sUIcidar enumerates configured application/browser paths through cHEga. Plain Discord tokens are extracted with MFA/token regexes; encrypted dQw4w9WgXcQ records are decoded, the Local State key is unwrapped with @primno/dpapi.unprotectData(CurrentUser), and AES-GCM tag/IV/ciphertext slices are processed. Tokens are validated against Discord /users/@me and used for billing/payment-sources and relationship queries. Tokens and account/friend/billing data are sent in webhook embeds.

faLar reads browser Local State os_crypt.encrypted_key, removes its five-byte prefix and launches a PowerShell ProtectedData.Unprotect command to recover the master key. QUErome copies Login Data, queries origin_url/username_value/password_value from logins, performs AES-GCM decryption and stages Passwords.txt. queRome processes Network/Cookies rows and archives recovered records. cheGa copies Web Data and extracts autofill rows.

deiCe obtains a GoFile upload server, posts a local createReadStream through form-data to uploadFile and returns downloadPage. Its fallback posts the file to a Discord webhook. queRome reports links and counts for cookies/passwords/autofills/wallet and Steam archives through Discord.

FalAr archives Exodus exodus.wallet; QueRome archives Steam config; CheGa scans Downloads/Documents/Desktop/OneDrive Desktop for sensitive filename words, excludes mp4, archives selected files and uploads them. The large wallet extension-target map and recursive copy/archive helpers are also present. Do not infer that every wallet map entry is reached: the small nikKi routine is a no-op.

NIKki fetches replacement source from a configured HTTPS endpoint, substitutes webhook/logout/QR placeholders and traverses Discord app/module directories to replace discord_desktop_core index.js. This is a module-tampering attempt; neither the fetched payload nor a successful replacement was observed.

sEnTimentos copies process.execPath into APPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup using fs.copyFileSync and path.join. If this source is run with ordinary Node, execPath denotes node.exe, not this script, so successful reactivation of the stealer is not established. No packaging evidence shows that it was compiled into a self-contained executable.

samples.marker_line: SEO doorway HTML: cloaked search redirects; narrow packing claim
samples.reason: The page is an SEO doorway titled Indexed rate and fully indexed rate. Its numeric-packed script selects visitors by search-engine referrer and query-parameter presence, redirects those visitors to an external finance/search page with encoded referrer and current-page information, and sends other visitors to a local 404. Concealment, selective diversion, the 404 decoy and keyword-stuffed filler establish traffic hijacking. No evidence establishes exploitation or the behavior of the remote destination; those are not needed for this verdict.
reverse_engineering: Wakjigtb parses a hash-delimited decimal string into characters with String.fromCharCode and inserts the result through document.write. The 1896-byte decoded stage defines encode/getRef/key and performs referrer-gated navigation.

The stage tests document.referrer for google., msn., yahoo., bing., altavista., aol. and ask. and looks for their query parameters. Matching traffic is assigned to an external /search.php destination. The extracted search term is not actually used; q is a fixed indexed-rate phrase.
key() hex-encodes getRef()+"|"+document.location+"|" into the outgoing r query parameter. Nonmatching traffic goes to http://<current hostname>/404.html.

JS-only document/window stubs verify Google/Yahoo query arrivals take the external branch, while an empty referrer and Google without a query take the 404 branch. The document writer output was decoded and evaluated against inert property-only stubs; no navigation or network activity occurred.

corrections.unsupported: The matcher requires only repeated additions of numeric-argument calls. This sample uses Base91 string-table indexes, and the square-sum control uses arithmetic. Neither establishes character-code semantics or concealment.
corrections.fix: Move the unchanged observation and exclusions to metadata/lang/source/syntax/call at notable. Equivalent regex grouping preserves all 130 raw spans in the original sample and five spans in each arithmetic control.
corrections.consumer: The exact evaluator consumer follows the moved ID and is renamed to numeric-helper-chains-near-eval. It now says co-occurrence and is suspicious instead of hostile: near_lines does not prove that helper results feed eval.

corrections.claim: Entire eval argument is Unicode escaped
corrections.unsupported: The existing matcher also accepts Function, including an uninvoked constructor, and only requires an eight-escape prefix.
corrections.fix: Rename and describe the same matcher as unicode-escape-prefix-code-argument. Retain suspicious severity and update the exact consumer.

corrections.claim: Hash decoder plus document.write is necessarily hostile
corrections.unsupported: The existing external packed-snippet fixture decodes alert('x'), while license-blob/decode-only and greeting controls show normal character-code uses. Source-plus-sink co-occurrence does not establish malicious content or a linked value.
corrections.fix: Keep the writer observation at suspicious and describe co-occurrence. Retain both hostile referrer-cloaking and traffic-diversion traits on the original malicious HTML and the external cloaked-redirect fixture.

corrections.claim: A quoted numeric list is an encoding operation
corrections.unsupported: Six hash-delimited decimal values show a source literal prefix. The matcher does not require an encoder.
corrections.fix: Move it unchanged from micro-behaviors/data/encode/charcode to metadata/lang/source/literal and update both exact consumers and the existing cases file.

corrections.claim: The literal arch is host discovery
corrections.unsupported: A standalone field-name literal is not an architecture query.
corrections.fix: Move the same literal observation to metadata/lang/source/literal; retain notable severity and update local host-field composites.

new_coverage: Calls through split addLocalFolder, writeZip and setAuthTag member names, all notable. Call syntax is required; concatenated API fragments used only as data are negative controls.

consumer_audit.reviewed: Inspected exact references and all old/new ancestor selectors before changing matching/severity. No consumer uses the old hash writer as a prerequisite. The numeric helper has one exact evaluator consumer; its unrelated Run/WSH siblings were retained.
consumer_audit.intentional_membership_changes: Generic numeric-call sums no longer satisfy broad string-obfuscation selectors. A bare arch literal no longer blocks vendor-API exceptions by masquerading as os/sysinfo, and a decimal string prefix no longer supplies encoding/crypto context to broad encode selectors. Preserving those unsupported implications would defeat the corrections. The source observations remain available under their precise metadata IDs.
consumer_audit.outside_batch_controls: Existing packed-snippet, decode-only, plain-write, cloaked-redirect, license-blob, plain-referrer-redirect, short greeting and chr quote controls were read and tested. The historical 90da828a7f86 credential-stealer review was inspected; original bytes were absent and forager --hash tried MalwareBazaar, Triage and Malshare without recovering them. No reconstructed file is represented as that original.

coverage_gaps: The npm package has two hostile findings, but they describe one exfiltration result and its install-hook context, not two independent attacks. The speed-test upload is ordinary generated-data traffic and must not be relabeled as theft.

The damaged obfuscated JavaScript has one hostile Discord-token-harvest trait and four suspicious obfuscation traits. Manual decoding establishes browser theft, uploads and tampering, but the current facts do not reconstruct the LZW/Base91/rotated table or expose the damaged source calls reliably. The three new neutral API observations recover supported mechanics. No duplicate hostile composite or sample-specific table index was added to meet a count. Successful JavaScript persistence is additionally unproven because the self-copy source is process.execPath.
The HTML has two distinct hostile results: search-referrer cloaking/404 decoy and traffic diversion. Decoder-only observation remains suspicious.
classifier_disagreements: Malicious npm: probability remains 0.9974145 and lvl -1, outside the calibrated alert grid, despite both retained hostile rules.
Malicious JavaScript: probability 0.968621 -> 0.9698371, lvl -1 before and after. This remains a classifier miss and a behavioral-objective coverage gap; scores were not tuned.
Malicious HTML: probability 0.96 -> 0.95, lvl 25 before and after. Both attack traits remain; reducing a generic decoder claim does not change the malicious judgment.

The installed scanner reports model feature spec v18 versus extractor v19. Initial validation-on scans were blocked by the installed scanner build lacking the already documented metadata/file/naming 101-rule budget; the actual before/after scans use CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 consistently. The selected source-matched release cleave admits that documented budget and is used for checks and final validation.

validation.order: Run as the final action after writing all judgment markers.

limits: All sample analysis was static or used inert bounded JS-only codec/effect stubs. No sample network activity, final remote payload, successful data export, live credential access or actual persistence was observed. External verdicts were not used as evidence.
